chapter_theme: Ainkurunuru 371 to 380, Othalanthaiyar's paalai decade of the mother's lament after her daughter's elopement (மகட்போக்கிய வழித் தாய் இரங்கு பத்து): the mother blesses the road, asks if she is remembered, curses the youth's mother and the fate that joined them, weeps over the doll and parrot and the toys left behind, grieves for the friend left alone, and ends saying she was mother only in name.

371.reading: The mother prays that rain may fall on the high hills where peacocks dance to the warriors' drumming, so that the wasteland her crescent-browed girl has gone through may be pleasant, the girl who made up her mind that this was the path of right.
371.nuance: The mother does not blame the girl: she grants that the daughter judged the going to be அறநெறி, the right way, and turns her grief into a wish for rain on the road. The peacocks dancing to a drum are the hill country's festivity imported into a paalai wish.

thinai_evidence.note: the girl has gone through the wasteland with her lover

thurai_akam.speaker: nartaay
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai; the decade's title (மகட்போக்கிய வழித் தாய் இரங்கு பத்து) names the mother lamenting after her daughter's elopement; she speaks a wish for the road, to no one named

372.reading: The mother asks whether her daughter, who crossed many rich hills with the youth of oaths who won her heart, while gossip rose in the noisy old town, thinks even of her.
372.nuance: என்னும் asks only for the least: not that the girl grieve, but that she remember her mother at all. The youth is named by his வஞ்சினம், the sworn word that persuaded the girl, so the mother places the cause of the going in speech.

thinai_evidence.note: the daughter has crossed the hills with the youth

thurai_akam.speaker: nartaay
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai; the decade's title (மகட்போக்கிய வழித் தாய் இரங்கு பத்து) names the mother lamenting after her daughter's elopement; the question is spoken aloud to no one named

iraicchi.act: the stag, just escaped from the tiger, calls its doe with its male voice to come and join it
iraicchi.sense: the youth's call drew the daughter into the same danger, so the mother sees on the road the very call that took her girl

373.reading: The mother wishes on the mother of the strong-bowed youth who led her daughter into the hot wasteland, where an old forked-horned stag that escaped a tiger's grip calls in its male voice for its doe to come to it, a grief that makes her weep each time she thinks of it.
373.nuance: The curse asks the other mother to suffer exactly what the speaker suffers (நினைத்தொறும் கலிழும்), so it is grief demanding a mirror rather than plain hatred. The stag that has just escaped death and at once calls its doe is the danger and the pull of the road in one image.

thinai_evidence.note: the youth has led the daughter into the hot waste

thurai_akam.speaker: nartaay
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai; the decade's title (மகட்போக்கிய வழித் தாய் இரங்கு பத்து) names the mother lamenting after her daughter's elopement; the curse names the youth's mother in the third person

374.reading: The mother, turning it over many times, says that her girl, whose hair is not yet long enough to be gathered into a knot, has crossed, guarded by the youth of fierce strength, a forest that even the male monkey does not know.
374.nuance: Hair too short for the knot (முடியகம் புகாக் கூந்தல்) is the mother's proof that the girl is still a child. Line 1's நல்லென் றூழ is hard to divide: it may be நல் என்று ஊழ (fate called good) or a self-description, so whether the mother consoles herself or despairs is open.

thinai_evidence.note: the girl has crossed the forest under the youth's guard

thurai_akam.speaker: nartaay
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai; the decade's title (மகட்போக்கிய வழித் தாய் இரங்கு பத்து) names the mother lamenting after her daughter's elopement; she speaks of the girl in the third person to no one named

comparisons.tenor: the daughter, called a green parrot

375.reading: The mother, troubled each time she sees them, says 'this is my doll's doll, this is the green parrot my green parrot raised', and asks whether her flower-eyed girl of the restless glance and bright brow has really gone.
375.nuance: The repetitions are built on two metaphors for the girl: she is herself the பாவை whose doll this is and the பைங்கிளி who reared this parrot, so each object the mother sees names the daughter twice. The doubling of words (பாவை பாவை, பைங்கிளி ... பைங்கிளி, காண்தொறும் காண்தொறும்) enacts the unbroken looking.

thurai_akam.speaker: nartaay
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai; the decade's title (மகட்போக்கிய வழித் தாய் இரங்கு பத்து) names the mother lamenting after her daughter's elopement; she speaks to herself over the girl's things

comparisons.tenor: the burning she wishes on fate

376.reading: The mother, though she weeps day after day, wishes that the loveless fate which came between, joined the simple flower-eyed girl to her lover and sent her off, throwing the great house of good deeds into uproar, may burn like a forest fire.
376.nuance: The curse falls not on the youth or the girl but on பால், the destiny that pairs lovers, and calls it அறனில் (without right). Set beside 371, where the girl judged the going அறநெறி, the decade puts the question of right inside the mother's own lament.

thinai_evidence.note: fate joined the girl to her lover and sent her away

thurai_akam.speaker: nartaay
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai; the decade's title (மகட்போக்கிய வழித் தாய் இரங்கு பத்து) names the mother lamenting after her daughter's elopement; the curse is spoken against fate, to no one named

377.reading: The mother says her daughter has surely gone through the wasteland where an elephant, weary and driven by thirst, breathes like a pipe played with the drums, leaving to them her ball, her doll and her playing pebbles.
377.nuance: எமக்கு ஒழித்தே makes the toys a bequest: what the girl leaves to her mother is her childhood, and the elephant's hard breathing measures the road she has gone to instead.

thinai_evidence.note: the thirsty waste of the road

thurai_akam.speaker: nartaay
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai; the decade's title (மகட்போக்கிய வழித் தாய் இரங்கு பத்து) names the mother lamenting after her daughter's elopement; she speaks of the girl in the third person to no one named

378.reading: The mother says that in the lonely evening, when the bat spreads its wings and rises to go, she does not grieve for the girl who has gone; she grieves for this one, the friend left without her honey-voiced companion, whose paired kohl eyes weep with her heart.
378.nuance: The turn 'not for her, but for this one' moves the mother's grief from the daughter to the friend who stays behind, so the loss is counted in the companion too. The bat setting out at dusk echoes the girl's going but does nothing a person of the situation does, so it stays scene.

thurai_akam.speaker: nartaay
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai; the decade's title (மகட்போக்கிய வழித் தாய் இரங்கு பத்து) names the mother lamenting after her daughter's elopement; she points to the friend (இவட்கு) as she speaks, so the hearer is someone else in the house

iraicchi.act: the bull elephants keep to their herd as they roam the grove
iraicchi.sense: even the elephants on her road stay with their herd, while the girl has left her own band of companions and their wedding for one man

379.reading: The mother wonders whether going in union with the man of the polished white spear, through the groves of the cold hills where herds of bull elephants roam, is sweeter to her daughter than enjoying a good wedding among her loving companions.
379.nuance: Unusually the mother imagines the girl's pleasure rather than her pain, and the road is a cool hill grove, not a burnt waste. The herd of elephants (இனக்களிறு) set against the girl's own band (ஆயம்) that she has left is what carries the reproach.

thinai_evidence.note: she has gone off in union with the man

thurai_akam.speaker: nartaay
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai; the decade's title (மகட்போக்கிய வழித் தாய் இரங்கு பத்து) names the mother lamenting after her daughter's elopement; she wonders aloud, to no one named

comparisons.tenor: the girl's smile, like a bud opening

380.reading: The mother says of the simple girl with pearl-white teeth and budding smile who went with him through the long waste: she herself only bore the name of mother, and surely it was the girl's playmates who gave her away.
380.nuance: கொடுத்தோர் is the word for giving a bride: the mother says the giving that should have been hers was done by the girl's companions, who knew and helped. Her self-belittling (தாயர் என்னும் பெயரே) is the grief of one stripped of her office.

thinai_evidence.note: the girl went with him through the waste

thurai_akam.speaker: nartaay
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai; the decade's title (மகட்போக்கிய வழித் தாய் இரங்கு பத்து) names the mother lamenting after her daughter's elopement; she speaks of the girl and of herself to no one named

links.note: Both wish the wasteland the girl has crossed with her lover cool with rain or cloud, in the same frame (...ஆகுக ... போகிய சுரனே); Kuruntokai's speaker is the foster mother, Ainkurunuru's the mother.
links.teaches: Kuruntokai's wish asks only shade, sand and cloud for a frightened road, while Ainkurunuru adds that the girl judged the going to be the path of right, so the same blessing formula could also carry the household's grudging moral consent to the elopement.

links.note: 371 says the girl went having judged this the path of right (அறநெறி); 376 calls the fate that joined and sent her without right (அறனில் பால்).
links.teaches: One decade by one poet lets the mother both concede that her daughter chose rightly and curse the joining as wrong, so the dispute over whether elopement is அறம் is staged inside a single lament rather than between mother and girl.

links.note: Both mothers wish on the mother who bore the youth the same grief they feel (Natrinai: எம்போல் பெரு விதுப்புறுக; Ainkurunuru: நினைத்தொறும் கலிழும் இடும்பை எய்துக).
links.teaches: Natrinai ties the wished grief to the sight of the girl's playmates at a festival, Ainkurunuru to every thought of the road, so the curse on the youth's mother was a set move whose point is to make the other mother feel exactly the speaker's own loss.

links.note: Akananuru 195's mother says the youth's mother will joyfully paint her walls for the couple's coming; Ainkurunuru 373's mother wishes that same woman grief.
links.teaches: Held together, the two poems show the bereaved mother's view of the other house in its two moods, envy of the joy it awaits and a curse that it should share her grief, so the youth's mother is a fixed counter-figure of this lament.

links.note: Both mothers weep each time they see what the girl left (காண்தொறும்): Ainkurunuru the doll and the parrot she reared, Natrinai the courtyard, the playmates and the nochchi.
links.teaches: Ainkurunuru stops at the doubled grief of looking, while Natrinai turns from the same sight to declare the girl faultless, so the scene of the left belongings could lead either to bare lament or to the mother's acquittal of her daughter.

links.note: Ainkurunuru 377 says the girl left her ball, doll and pebbles to us; Akananuru 369 says the parrot will not drink and the doll gets no offering since she went.
links.teaches: In Akananuru the left things mourn with the household, while in Ainkurunuru they are a bequest the girl hands back with her childhood, so the same toys can be made grieving witnesses or the plain sign that childhood is over.

links.note: Both use the turn 'I do not grieve that she went; I grieve for...' (நோவேன் ... நோவல்): Akananuru 63 for the girl's night in a robbers' hamlet, Ainkurunuru 378 for the friend left behind.
links.teaches: The 'not this but that' turn of the mother's lament could redirect grief either to the girl's hardships on the road or, as in Ainkurunuru, to the companion at home, so the lament counts the friend's loss as a second wound of the elopement.

links.note: Akananuru 369's girl refused the rich wedding her kin were preparing (தமர்மணன் அயரவும் ஒல்லாள்); Ainkurunuru 379's mother asks whether going with him is sweeter than a good wedding among her companions.
links.teaches: Akananuru states the refusal of the home wedding as a grievance, and Ainkurunuru asks the question that refusal implies, whether the road was sweeter to the girl, so the mother's lament moves from blaming the choice to trying to imagine the girl's own preference.

links.note: Akananuru 263's mother says that had she known she would gladly have married the girl to him in her rich house; Ainkurunuru 380's mother says she was only mother in name and the playmates gave her away.
links.teaches: Read together the two show the mother grieving a lost office as much as a lost daughter: the giving of the bride that 263 wishes she had performed, 380 says was done behind her back by the girl's companions.

links.note: Akananuru 315's mother saw the girl's hair curl and breasts swell and blames herself for not guarding her; Ainkurunuru 374's mother says the girl's hair was not yet long enough to be knotted.
links.teaches: On one reading the two mothers read the same hair in opposite ways, as a sign of womanhood missed in Akananuru and as proof of childhood in Ainkurunuru, so the lament can either confess overlooked signs or deny that there were any.

links.note: Ainkurunuru 372 asks whether the girl thinks even of her mother (என்னும் உள்ளினள் கொல்லோ); Akananuru 383 says the girl never thought of the mother who raised her; gossip rises in both.
links.teaches: What Ainkurunuru leaves as an anxious question Akananuru settles as a charge, so the pair shows the mother's doubt about being remembered hardening, in the longer poem, into reproach.

source_issues: Decade title as printed reads மக்ட் போக்கிய வழித் தாயிரங்கு பத்து; மக்ட் is a misprint for மகட் (மகட்போக்கிய).
374 line 1: நல்லென் றூழ is hard to divide (நல் என்று ஊழ, or a form of நல்லேன்); the reading is marked uncertain.
